title: Observe, govern, secure
brief: Agents run on many platforms, yet an administrator must still see, govern and secure them. Decide how each agent joins the control plane and which loop keeps it healthy after launch.

blocks.text: Agent 365 is a control plane, not a runtime

blocks.md:
Agent 365 is Microsoft's control plane for agents with three pillars [[r12]]. **Observe** covers the agent registry, the agent map, adoption and health. **Govern** covers lifecycle, access and compliance through the registry in the Microsoft 365 admin center, Entra and Purview. **Secure** covers Entra risk-based access, Purview DLP and information protection, and Defender threat detection.

It reached general availability on 2026-05-01 for the Commercial segment and is licensed per user. At least one user needs a qualifying Agent 365 license. It is included in Microsoft 365 E7 and is an add-on to E5, A5 or Business Premium. The overview page carried no price on 2026-10-13, so quote none. Agent 365 is also the unified registry, while Entra stays the identity foundation [[r29]]. The capabilities announced as the Microsoft Entra Agent Registry continue: agent identity capabilities stay in Entra Agent ID and the registration APIs remain supported, but the full inventory, including agents without an Entra identity, is in Agent 365.

blocks.title: Many platforms, one registry
blocks.alt: Foundry, Copilot Studio, framework-built and cross-cloud agents all feed the agent registry, which supports observe, govern and secure.

items.symptom: An agent is missing from the inventory
items.cause: Native integration covers Microsoft platforms and supported partners. Framework agents need the SDK and other clouds need registry sync
items.fix: Pick the join path from the dial board and check the registry after a test run.

items.symptom: One Copilot Studio agent shows up twice in the registry
items.cause: A Copilot Studio agent can appear under more than one registry type by design
items.fix: Deduplicate by agent id, not by row, before you report counts.

items.symptom: New code instruments with the Agent 365 Observability SDK
items.cause: That SDK and its packages are deprecated for new work

items.symptom: A team-workflow agent is promised as GA
items.cause: Agents in team workflows with their own access were public preview at the 2026-05-01 announcement
items.fix: Confirm the current status and accept preview terms before production [[r20]].

items.symptom: A team expects the SDK to host the agent
items.cause: The Agent 365 SDK does not build, host, orchestrate or run tools
items.fix: Host the agent on a runtime from level 1 and add the SDK for identity, tooling and notifications [[r13]].

blocks.title: GA and preview inside one announcement
blocks.md: At the 2026-05-01 announcement, agents working on behalf of users and agents behind the scenes with their own access were GA. Agents in team workflows with their own access were public preview. Discovery of local and shadow agents through Defender and Intune was announced as preview. Agent user accounts and notifications need the Frontier preview program. Checked 2026-10-13.

The registry lives in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Agents, All Agents, Registry [[r16]]. It has four types: Microsoft agents, external partner-built agents, published by your org and shared by creator.

items.title: Go deeper: what the SDK adds

blocks.md: The Agent 365 SDK ships Python, JavaScript and .NET packages for identity, tooling and notifications [[r13]]. Tooling means governed Work IQ MCP servers for Mail, Calendar, Word, SharePoint and Teams. It is not the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK. Notifications need an agent user account and the Frontier preview program. Three paths exist: native integration, the SDK for framework-built agents (Microsoft 365 Agents SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, Microsoft Agent Framework, LangChain, CrewAI, LlamaIndex) and registry synchronization for platforms such as Vertex AI and AWS Bedrock.

items.title: Go deeper: the Foundry Control Plane proxy

blocks.md: You can register a custom agent that runs elsewhere in the Foundry Control Plane, and Foundry puts API Management in front as a proxy for access control and monitoring [[r23]]. For A2A agents the default agent card path is `/.well-known/agent-card.json`. An AI gateway is free to set up. This is a Foundry layer. Agent 365 is the Microsoft 365 layer that ingests agents from Foundry and elsewhere.

quiz.q: A team assumes adopting the Agent 365 SDK will host their LangChain agent. What is true?
options: It adds identity, governed tooling and notifications, but you still host and run the agent
It hosts and scales the agent inside the Microsoft 365 tenant
It replaces the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK for building agents
It runs the agent's tools in a sandbox that Agent 365 manages
quiz.explain: The Agent 365 SDK provides identity, governed Work IQ tooling and notifications. It does not build, host, orchestrate or run tools, and it is not the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK.

quiz.q: Match each situation to the way the agent joins the control plane.

pairs.l: A Microsoft platform agent or a supported partner agent
A LangChain agent you host and can change
An agent on Vertex AI or AWS Bedrock
A custom agent elsewhere that needs gateway access control

quiz.explain: Microsoft platforms and supported partners integrate natively. Framework-built agents add the SDK. Connected platforms such as Vertex AI and Bedrock use registry sync. A custom agent elsewhere can be registered in the Foundry Control Plane, which proxies it through API Management.

quiz.q: A platform team wants agents that join team workflows with their own access in production, because Agent 365 is GA. Which risk statement is right?
options: They are GA with the rest of the product, so nothing more is needed before production use
They need Entra P2 before they can run at all
They only run as Foundry hosted agents
They were public preview on 2026-05-01, so confirm status and accept preview terms
quiz.explain: The announcement split modes: delegated and behind-the-scenes agents were GA and team-workflow agents with their own access were public preview. A GA product label does not make every mode GA. The Entra P2 and hosted-only claims have no support in the sources.

takeaways: Agent 365 observes, governs and secures agents. It does not build or host them
Native and sync add inventory, the SDK adds code-level capabilities, and each needs the right code ownership
A GA product can hold preview modes, so check each mode and date
Use the Microsoft OpenTelemetry Distro, not the deprecated Observability SDK
